added.description:
About Rebill

Rebill is the financial infrastructure platform for the Americas.

The companies shaping software, AI, travel, and digital services use Rebill to operate across Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, and the United States.

Rebill brings local payments, installments, recurring billing, stablecoin rails, treasury, global payouts, and financial operations into one platform built for how money actually works across the Americas.

Every market is different. Rebill makes the infrastructure consistent. Engineering, finance, and operations teams can manage local currency acceptance, market-specific payment behavior, funds, and financial workflows from the same platform.

Companies can launch in Latin America in as little as a day and expand across markets without rebuilding their financial stack country by country.

Built locally. Designed to scale globally.

Rebill is backed by leading global investors such as Tiger Global, Y Combinator (W22), Soma Capital and SV Angel, and angels including Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) and Arash Ferdowsi (Dropbox).

About the role

Engineering

You run engineering day to day: delivery, reliability, and the technical bar of everything we ship.

Rebill processes real money across six markets on its own infrastructure. Event-driven microservices on a message bus, Kubernetes across Azure and AWS, infrastructure as code, and smart routing across a different set of local acquirers in every country. Card data lives in an isolated, tokenized environment.

You lead a small in-house team alongside external engineering partners, and you report to the CTO, who owns architecture, security, and the technical relationship with our acquirers. You own everything between that and production.

This is a hands-on seat. You will review pull requests and write code in your first year. If you have not been close to a codebase in the last two years, this is not the right seat for you.

Why this role exists

Rebill launched its own payment infrastructure in September 2025, starting with Argentina. In one year it went from that single market to six.

That platform was built fast by very few people. The next stage is different: more volume, more acquirers, more markets, and merchants whose finance teams depend on us settling correctly every day. That needs someone whose full-time job is making the platform reliable, cheap to extend, and predictable to ship on.

What you will own

Reliability. Uptime, incident response, observability, and the performance of payment routing. When approval rates drop in one market at two in the morning, you are the person who knows why.
Delivery. The quarterly technical roadmap, release cadence, and the honesty of our dates. Engineering commitments that hold are worth more than ambitious ones that do not.
